narr: An upper level system coincided with abundant atmospheric moisture across the Texas Panhandle on the evening of the 24th. This resulted in scattered thunderstorms that eventually grew into widespread thunderstorm activity. A few storms became strong to severe thunderstorms that produced heavy rainfall, severe wind gusts, and a localized occurrence of hail up to ping pong ball size. The biggest hazard that occurred during this event was the flash flooding that occurred in the Amarillo and Canyon areas. The widespread thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall and storms continued to move over the same locations. Flash flooding resulted in stalled cars and flooded and closed roadways. Flooding in Palo Duro Canyon State Park resulted in flooded roads and a few of the campsites had to be evacuated.
ev: Heavy rainfall and multiple rounds of rain brought flash flooding to north central Randall County. Vehicles were stalled in the fast moving flood waters near the US-87 and I-27 interchange. Some roads were also closed across the city of Canyon.
One to two feet of water occurred over some bridges in Palo Duro Canyon State Park with roads being closed. Campsites were evacuated.
